meta.title: SEM features of Si/C battery electrodes: reference data
notes: Numeric values are illustrative literature ranges for Si/graphite-type anodes at room temperature, not universal acceptance limits.
Evidence: High = widely reported and mechanistically clear; Medium = reported but system-dependent; Low = hypothesis needing a second technique.
indicator_of_properties comes only from the property-index table; verify_methods is keyword matching on verify_with_text.
Verified against OpenAlex on 2026-10-03; see verification_method, references, change_log and deleted_items.

verification_method.source: OpenAlex (title/abstract level; no full text read)
verification_method.queries: about 30 keyword searches sorted by citation count (Si anodes, Si/C, Si-graphite, SEI, binders, porosity/tortuosity/calendering, Li plating, drying cracks, tomography, SiOx, etc.)
verification_method.reference_set: 100 highly cited relevant works (tier core_top100) plus 6 lower-cited supplementary works for niche claims; see references[]

status_values.confirmed: claim consistent with retrieved literature, unchanged
status_values.corrected: claim kept but wording/number changed or unsupported detail removed
status_values.partially_confirmed: core idea supported, specifics not found; kept with note
status_values.method_guidance_retained: instrument/technique advice not testable from abstracts; retained and flagged

verification_method.policy: Features with no supporting work retrieved were deleted (D6, F1); unsupported numeric thresholds/examples were removed; deleted items are preserved in deleted_items for restoration.

categories.name: B. Carbon phase and conductive network
C. Binder, interphase and particle contacts

features.name: Si primary particle size
features.how_to_recognise_and_best_mode: Bright (high-Z) particles in BSE; cross-section preferred. InLens/SE for small particles.
features.what_to_measure: Equivalent-circle diameter D10/D50/D90 from ≥200 particles; fraction of particles above a stated size; distribution width.
features.verify_with_text: TEM for particle/crystallite morphology; XRD–Scherrer only for crystallite/coherent-domain size; laser diffraction for powder/agglomerate size distribution (not a substitute for single-particle SEM).
features.favorable_state: Crystalline Si primary particle size ≲100–150 nm; narrow distribution.
features.unfavorable_state: Solid particles ≳150 nm up to µm; broad distribution with large outliers.
features.linked_properties_and_mechanism: Cycle life, capacity retention, first-cycle efficiency (ICE). Si expands ~280–300% on full lithiation; sufficiently large crystalline Si particles may crack, expose fresh surface, promote SEI growth, and lose electrical contact. The critical size is system- and constraint-dependent, not a universal cutoff.

verification.note: In situ TEM shows a critical diameter of about 150 nm on first lithiation (cracking above, none below); ~300% Si expansion is consistent across reviews; micrometre-sized Si is reported to pulverise.

features.name: Si phase fraction and dispersion
features.how_to_recognise_and_best_mode: BSE area-fraction of the bright phase; map several fields across the full thickness.
features.what_to_measure: Bright-phase area fraction (≥5 fields), nearest-neighbour distance, cluster size, local-fraction variance.
features.verify_with_text: EDS (Si map), ICP/TGA for Si wt%; use matched imaging conditions and calibration before treating BSE area fraction as quantitative.
features.favorable_state: Uniform dispersion; no clusters; spread matches the intended Si loading.
features.unfavorable_state: Agglomerates of several µm or more; Si-rich and Si-poor zones; large Si-free regions.
features.linked_properties_and_mechanism: Usable capacity (Si up to ~3500–4200 mAh/g vs graphite 372), local current and swelling uniformity. Clusters create local stress hot spots; area fraction approximates volume fraction only with representative sampling.

verification.note: Si capacity of ~3579 (Li15Si4) to ~4200 mAh/g (Li22Si5) versus graphite 372 mAh/g matches retrieved abstracts. BSE area-fraction guidance is a method recommendation not testable from abstracts.

features.name: Si particle shape and internal structure
features.how_to_recognise_and_best_mode: SE/InLens at high magnification; BSE shows internal Si/pore contrast. Cross-section or fractured particle needed for internal view.
features.what_to_measure: Aspect ratio, sphericity, internal pore fraction, pore size, wall/shell thickness, edge sharpness.
features.verify_with_text: TEM for internal structure; N₂ adsorption/BET for powder surface area and pore statistics, with appropriate model limitations.
features.favorable_state: Porous, hollow, nano-grained or rounded particles with internal free volume.
features.unfavorable_state: Dense micrometre-scale Si particles (prone to pulverisation).
features.linked_properties_and_mechanism: Expansion tolerance and cycle life, balanced against tap density. Internal voids and porosity absorb part of the volume change; dense micrometre-scale particles pulverise more readily.

verification.note: Hollow, porous and yolk-shell Si are well supported; the angular/sharp-corner stress-concentrator statement was removed.

features.category: B. Carbon phase and conductive network
features.name: Graphite / carbon host morphology
features.how_to_recognise_and_best_mode: SE/ETD; cross-section for packing. Flake, spherical (rounded), potato-shaped or amorphous hard-carbon particles.
features.what_to_measure: D50, aspect ratio, sphericity, surface roughness, visible edge-plane exposure.
features.verify_with_text: Laser diffraction, BET, tap density, Raman
features.favorable_state: Rounded/spherical particles; published spherical-graphite studies use x50 of roughly 11–18 µm (an example, not a universal optimum); smooth surface with limited fines.
features.unfavorable_state: High-aspect-ratio sharp flakes, many exposed edges, very fine fragments.
features.linked_properties_and_mechanism: Packing density, rate capability, ICE. Edge planes and fines raise surface area, so more SEI and Li loss in the first cycle; flakes also orient strongly during calendering.

verification.note: Particle-size distribution, platelet orientation and edge-plane exposure (initial irreversible capacity) are supported, the latter only by low-citation supplementary works; flake behaviour in calendering is supported generally.

features.category: B. Carbon phase and conductive network
features.name: Carbon coating on Si or composite particles
features.how_to_recognise_and_best_mode: Shell visible at high magnification on fractured or milled particles (InLens); thin nanometre-scale shells are often not resolvable by SEM.
features.what_to_measure: Coverage fraction, continuity, and cracked/peeled areas. Shell thickness should be measured primarily by TEM; SEM can provide a high-magnification continuity screen, but very thin shells are often not reliably resolved.
features.verify_with_text: TEM, Raman (D/G ratio), TGA, XPS.
features.favorable_state: Continuous, conformal, well-bonded coating; thickness confirmed by TEM where relevant.
features.unfavorable_state: Patchy, cracked or peeling shell; or overly thick and dense.
features.linked_properties_and_mechanism: Electronic conductivity, SEI stability, ICE, and rate. A good shell can reduce direct electrolyte exposure; an overly thick or rigid shell may fracture during expansion and add transport resistance. Effects depend on shell chemistry, porosity, and mechanical properties.

verification.note: Carbon/graphene shells improving Si stability are well supported; all numeric thickness thresholds were removed.

features.category: B. Carbon phase and conductive network
features.name: Void / buffer space in engineered composites
features.how_to_recognise_and_best_mode: Cross-section or broken particles: gap between Si core and shell (yolk–shell), internal cavities (pomegranate-type).
features.what_to_measure: Void-to-Si volume ratio, gap thickness, fraction of intact shells.
features.verify_with_text: FIB-SEM tomography, TEM, tap density
features.favorable_state: Void sized to accommodate the expected Si expansion while preserving shell integrity; because fully lithiated Si expands by ~280–300%, a void of about 3× the Si volume would be needed for complete accommodation at full lithiation (less when Si utilisation is limited); this is an idealised design reference, not a universal optimum.
features.unfavorable_state: No void (tight shell fractures) or oversized voids (low density, low volumetric capacity).
features.linked_properties_and_mechanism: Trade-off between cycle life and volumetric energy density. Void space can accommodate Si expansion, but the required amount depends on Si utilization, shell mechanics, pore compressibility, SEI growth, and electrolyte occupation.

verification.note: Yolk-shell, empty-space and pomegranate designs and the density trade-off are well supported; void ratio re-derived from expansion.

features.category: B. Carbon phase and conductive network
features.name: Conductive additives (carbon black, CNT, graphene)
features.how_to_recognise_and_best_mode: InLens/SE at high magnification. Carbon black: spheres fused into chain-like aggregates; CNT: fibres; graphene: crumpled sheets.
features.what_to_measure: Network connectivity (continuous paths), aggregate size, coverage of Si surfaces, bundle size.
features.verify_with_text: Four-probe/ electrode conductivity, EIS, Raman
features.favorable_state: Continuous, well-dispersed network contacting Si and carbon particles.
features.unfavorable_state: Large aggregates, CNT bundles, Si particles with no conductive contact.
features.linked_properties_and_mechanism: Electronic conductivity, rate capability, capacity utilization. Isolated Si becomes electrically dead; additive clumps waste volume and add no connectivity.

verification.note: Hybrid CNT/carbon conductive networks around Si are supported; size ranges removed.

features.category: C. Binder, interphase and particle contacts
features.name: Binder distribution and bridging
features.how_to_recognise_and_best_mode: Thin film or bridges between particles; difficult to image directly. PVDF may be assessed with F as an auxiliary signal (in cycled electrodes F can also come from LiPF₆ residue or SEI); Na is relevant only for sodium-containing CMC forms. O is non-specific and EDS is generally only supportive for dilute binder mapping.
features.what_to_measure: Fraction of contacts bridged, thickness of any top-surface skin, binder signal profile from foil to surface.
features.verify_with_text: peel/adhesion test, FTIR/Raman mapping, XPS, or ToF-SIMS; EDS line profiles are auxiliary and require controls.
features.favorable_state: Thin, uniform film bridging Si and carbon; uniform through thickness.
features.unfavorable_state: Pooling; binder enriched at the top surface (drying migration) and depleted at the foil; thick insulating films.
features.linked_properties_and_mechanism: Adhesion/cohesion, cycle life, resistance. Si-compatible binders (e.g., PAA, CMC, alginate) hold particles during swelling; migration causes delamination.

verification.note: Binder transport to the surface during drying with loss of adhesion is directly reported (W2972127671); PAA, CMC and alginate are supported Si binders.

features.category: C. Binder, interphase and particle contacts
features.name: SEI / surface film (cycled samples)
features.how_to_recognise_and_best_mode: Smoothed particle surfaces, filled pores, nodular or 'cauliflower' deposits in SE/InLens. Thickness is not reliably measurable by SEM.
features.what_to_measure: Fraction of pores occluded, surface-film coverage and roughness, change vs pristine at the same location.
features.verify_with_text: XPS, cryo-TEM, EIS, FTIR
features.favorable_state: A thin, relatively uniform, and stable film; thickness and composition should be confirmed by cryo-TEM/XPS rather than inferred from routine SEM.
features.unfavorable_state: Thick, rough, nodular, growing with cycling; cracking and reforming on Si.
features.linked_properties_and_mechanism: Coulombic efficiency, impedance growth, capacity fade, and electrolyte consumption. Si surface rupture can repeatedly expose fresh surface and promote SEI growth. Beam, vacuum, solvent, and air exposure can alter the film.

verification.note: SEI growth/instability on Si, characterisation by cryo-STEM/XPS/NMR/FIB-SEM, and thickness not being an SEM measurement are consistent with retrieved works.

features.category: C. Binder, interphase and particle contacts
features.name: Interparticle contact quality (Si–carbon, carbon–carbon)
features.how_to_recognise_and_best_mode: ETD/BSE cross-section: dark halos or gaps around particles indicate lost contact.
features.what_to_measure: Fraction of interface length with a visible gap, gap width, fraction of isolated particles, coordination number.
features.verify_with_text: EIS, electrode conductivity
features.favorable_state: Gap-free, intimate contacts; every Si particle touching carbon.
features.unfavorable_state: Gaps or halos around Si; isolated particles; delaminated shells.
features.linked_properties_and_mechanism: Internal resistance, inactive (dead) Si, capacity fade, local polarization.

verification.note: Loss of electrical contact and 3D particle failure in Si-C composite electrodes are reported.

features.name: Electrode porosity
features.how_to_recognise_and_best_mode: Black pore regions in ETD/BSE cross-section (carbon is dark grey in BSE); epoxy infiltration helps separate pores from carbon. ETD shadowing exaggerates pore area.
features.what_to_measure: Pore area fraction (≥5–10 fields, consistent threshold), compared with mass/thickness-based porosity; mean pore size.
features.verify_with_text: mass/thickness porosity, Hg porosimetry where appropriate, or FIB-SEM 3D. ETD/BSE black area is not porosity by itself; perform threshold-sensitivity analysis.
features.favorable_state: A system-dependent target range; about 25–40% can be used as an example for some pre-cycled graphite/Si–graphite anodes, but porosity must be evaluated with areal capacity, thickness, compaction density, pore connectivity, and wetting.
features.unfavorable_state: Very low porosity may limit electrolyte access and swelling accommodation; very high porosity can reduce energy density and mechanical contact. No universal cutoffs apply across electrode designs.
features.linked_properties_and_mechanism: Ion transport (rate), electrolyte uptake, energy density, swelling accommodation.

verification.note: Porosity affects rate/plating (26% vs 47% graphite anodes tested) and should be assessed with several methods. 25–40% remains an illustrative example only.

features.name: Pore size distribution and connectivity
features.how_to_recognise_and_best_mode: Cross-section; best by FIB-SEM tomography. Isolated closed voids vs connected channels.
features.what_to_measure: Pore-size distribution (µm range), connected-pore fraction, geometric tortuosity, bottleneck size.
features.verify_with_text: FIB-SEM 3D reconstruction, EIS (tortuosity), Hg porosimetry
features.favorable_state: Interconnected pores with a system-appropriate size distribution and low tortuosity.
features.unfavorable_state: Isolated voids; large voids comparable to particle size; narrow bottlenecks.
features.linked_properties_and_mechanism: Rate capability, fast-charge Li-plating risk, and electrolyte wetting. Interpret together with areal capacity, thickness, compaction density, and through-thickness tortuosity.

verification.note: Tortuosity and 3D pore networks from tomography are well supported; the size range was removed.

features.name: Particle orientation / anisotropy
features.how_to_recognise_and_best_mode: Cross-section; flakes lying parallel to the current collector versus more random or tilted orientations.
features.what_to_measure: Orientation-angle distribution relative to the foil normal (image structure tensor); orientation index.
features.verify_with_text: XRD orientation index, recognizing that XRD and image-based orientation probe different length scales.
features.favorable_state: More isotropic or tilted flake-orientation distribution; the optimum is system-dependent and should be checked with tortuosity and rate testing.
features.unfavorable_state: Strong alignment parallel to the foil may increase transport anisotropy in some electrodes, but it is not universally unfavorable.
features.linked_properties_and_mechanism: Through-plane Li⁺ transport, plating risk, and anisotropic swelling. Effects also depend on pore structure, graphite crystallographic texture, compaction, and electrolyte wetting.

verification.note: Platelet alignment affects rate performance (magnetically aligned graphite); effects are system dependent as already stated.

features.name: Calendering damage and packing density
features.how_to_recognise_and_best_mode: Cross-section: crushed or cracked graphite flakes, split secondary particles, closed pores.
features.what_to_measure: Fraction of fractured particles, closed-pore fraction, packing density vs target.
features.verify_with_text: Electrode density, BET, tap density
features.favorable_state: Intact particles, open pores at the target density.
features.unfavorable_state: Crushed/cracked particles, delaminated secondary Si/C particles, closed pores.
features.linked_properties_and_mechanism: Energy density, rate capability, fresh-surface area and extra SEI, and Si-composite integrity. Fresh-surface area is not measured directly by D4; BET can assist for powders but does not equal electrochemical active area in a working electrode.

verification.note: Calendering microstructure evolution and calendering-compatible Si-graphite designs are reported.

features.name: Coating thickness and uniformity
features.how_to_recognise_and_best_mode: Cross-section at multiple positions; surface profile.
features.what_to_measure: Thickness at ≥10 positions, coefficient of variation, roughness (Ra), edge build-up.
features.verify_with_text: Micrometer, profilometry
features.favorable_state: Low variation; the acceptable limit depends on coating method, loading, and cell design.
features.unfavorable_state: Wedge profile, ridges, thick edges, blade/slot-die streaks.
features.linked_properties_and_mechanism: Local loading and current distribution, plating risk, capacity variation between cells.

verification.note: Process-dependent coating uniformity is supported; quantitative CV limit and plating link were not found.

features.name: Electrode cracking (drying or cycling)
features.how_to_recognise_and_best_mode: Top view and cross-section: mud-crack network; orientation and depth.
features.what_to_measure: Crack areal density, width (µm), depth as fraction of thickness, whether cracks reach the foil.
features.verify_with_text: Optical microscopy, adhesion test, EIS
features.favorable_state: Low crack density; no large-area through-thickness cracks; cracks do not cause obvious loss of contact or delamination.
features.unfavorable_state: High-density or through-thickness cracks reaching the foil, especially when accompanied by delamination or contact loss.
features.linked_properties_and_mechanism: Electronic connectivity, delamination, capacity fade. Drying cracks form above a critical thickness; cycling cracks come from swelling.

verification.note: Thickness-dependent drying cracks (anodes and thick cathodes) and cracking of cycled Si-based films are reported.

features.name: Current-collector interface / delamination
features.how_to_recognise_and_best_mode: Cross-section at the foil: gap between coating and foil.
features.what_to_measure: Gap length / interface length (%), gap width, foil roughness.
features.verify_with_text: Peel test, interfacial EIS
features.favorable_state: Continuous intimate contact with the foil.
features.unfavorable_state: Lifted coating, gaps, binder-poor foil interface.
features.linked_properties_and_mechanism: Adhesion, interfacial resistance, sudden capacity loss.

verification.note: Loss of adhesion linked to binder transport during drying is reported; direct foil-interface delamination imaging studies were not retrieved.

features.name: Si particle fracture / pulverization
features.how_to_recognise_and_best_mode: Cracks through bright particles, shattered fragments, loss of sharp outlines. Compare the same region against a pristine sample.
features.what_to_measure: Fraction of Si particles with cracks (≥100 particles), crack density, and fragment size.
features.verify_with_text: SEM/TEM statistics under matched preparation; XRD may assess crystallinity changes but does not directly quantify particle fracture; EIS is complementary.
features.favorable_state: Intact particles after the intended cycle count.
features.unfavorable_state: Widespread cracking and fragmentation.
features.linked_properties_and_mechanism: Capacity fade, impedance rise, isolated Si, fresh surface for SEI regrowth.

verification.note: Cracking/pulverisation of Si particles on lithiation is directly observed in situ and in composite electrodes.

features.name: Electrode thickness swelling (cycled vs pristine)
features.how_to_recognise_and_best_mode: Cross-section thickness at the same state of charge; residual swelling after delithiation is most informative.
features.what_to_measure: Δt/t₀, reversible versus irreversible part, and uniformity across the electrode.
features.verify_with_text: cell-level thickness gauge, dilatometry, or matched-state cross-sectional measurements.
features.favorable_state: Swelling consistent with the Si fraction and electrode constraint;
features.unfavorable_state: High-Si, high-utilization, or weakly constrained electrodes may show tens of percent or more expansion; irreversible growth reflects SEI, pore rearrangement, delamination, and residual deformation.
features.linked_properties_and_mechanism: Volumetric energy density, cell stack pressure and deformation, contact loss, porosity loss. Note: material volume expansion (Si ~280–300%; porous Si designs report apparent particle expansion as low as ~40%) differs from electrode thickness swelling, which is also governed by porosity, binder and constraint.

verification.note: Electrode swelling versus material expansion is supported; graphite expansion figure removed.

features.name: Pore clogging / densification by decomposition products
features.how_to_recognise_and_best_mode: Cycled cross-section: pores filled with fine deposits, especially near the separator side.
features.what_to_measure: Porosity change versus pristine, fraction of filled pores, and depth profile.
features.verify_with_text: cross-sectional SEM/FIB-SEM 3D reconstruction or Hg porosimetry for pore changes; EDS for elemental gradients; XPS depth profiling or ToF-SIMS for surface-film chemistry, with sputtering artefacts considered.
features.favorable_state: Open pore network retained.
features.unfavorable_state: Surface-side pores filled; strong porosity gradient.
features.linked_properties_and_mechanism: Rate loss, impedance growth, plating risk.

verification.note: SEI densification/progressive SEI growth into Si electrodes is reported; separator-side pore filling profiles were not directly found.

features.name: Lithium plating / dendrites
features.how_to_recognise_and_best_mode: Mossy, whisker or filament deposits or smooth granular deposits on the surface. Requires air-free transfer.
features.what_to_measure: Coverage area fraction, morphology class, deposit thickness, and penetration toward the separator.
features.verify_with_text: cryo-/air-free SEM/TEM, XPS or ToF-SIMS; titration gas chromatography (titration GC, H₂ from Li + H₂O) can quantify metallic Li. Routine EDS generally cannot reliably detect Li.
features.favorable_state: None.
features.unfavorable_state: Any visible plating; mossy or whisker growth.
features.linked_properties_and_mechanism: Safety (short circuit), 'dead' lithium and capacity loss, low Coulombic efficiency. Linked to high rate, low temperature, high loading and poor pore transport.

verification.note: Li plating on graphite (dendrite/moss morphologies, fast charge, low temperature, porosity) is well supported; diameter range removed. Titration-GC and air-free transfer statements are method guidance.

features.name: Through-thickness degradation gradient
features.how_to_recognise_and_best_mode: Cycled cross-section: different crack density, swelling or film thickness from foil to separator side.
features.what_to_measure: Profiles of crack density, porosity, Si fracture fraction, and film coverage versus depth.
features.verify_with_text: cross-sectional SEM/FIB-SEM for cracks and pores; EDS for elemental gradients; XPS depth profiling or ToF-SIMS for film-composition gradients, with sputtering artefacts considered.
features.favorable_state: Approximately uniform through thickness.
features.unfavorable_state: Strong gradient, for example worse near the separator or foil, especially when reproducible across fields and samples.
features.linked_properties_and_mechanism: Current distribution and local over-use; points to transport limitations or binder migration.

verification.note: Binder migration and heterogeneous SEI growth support depth gradients; full depth-profile studies were not retrieved.

features.name: Carbon shell / coating failure (cycled)
features.how_to_recognise_and_best_mode: Broken, peeled or open shells exposing bright Si in BSE; collapsed voids.
features.what_to_measure: Fraction of broken shells, void collapse fraction, exposed-Si area.
features.verify_with_text: TEM, XPS
features.favorable_state: Intact shells.
features.unfavorable_state: Cracked or peeled shells with exposed Si.
features.linked_properties_and_mechanism: SEI regrowth, falling Coulombic efficiency, fade.

verification.note: Carbon coating role and coating-type differences are supported; direct shell-failure statistics were not found.

features.name: Foreign deposits on the anode (e.g., cathode transition metals)
features.how_to_recognise_and_best_mode: EDS-detectable Mn/Ni/Co or other metals on the anode surface; bright particles in BSE.
features.what_to_measure: Metal signal map, deposit size and density.
features.verify_with_text: EDS, XPS, ICP of washed electrode
features.favorable_state: None.
features.unfavorable_state: Metal deposits on or in the SEI.
features.linked_properties_and_mechanism: SEI destabilization, extra Li loss, faster fade.

verification.note: Transition-metal dissolution and cell degradation are supported; mapped to cycle life rather than safety.

features.name: Copper foil corrosion / pitting
features.how_to_recognise_and_best_mode: Foil surface or cross-section under the coating: pits, roughened or dissolved regions.
features.what_to_measure: Pit density and depth, foil thickness loss.
features.verify_with_text: EDS (Cu), EIS
features.favorable_state: Smooth intact foil.
features.unfavorable_state: Pitted or thinned foil, Cu deposits elsewhere in the cell.
features.linked_properties_and_mechanism: Interfacial resistance, short-circuit risk (after over-discharge).

verification.note: Cu current-collector corrosion in the over-discharged state is reported; pit/thickness-loss metrics not found.

properties.name: Cycle life / capacity retention
properties.key_indicators_text: Si particle size and fracture (A1, E1), carbon-shell integrity (B2, E6), Si–carbon contact (C3), binder bridging (C1), electrode cracking (D7), anode metal deposits (F2).
properties.direction_of_effect: Larger or fractured Si, broken shells, more cracks and contact gaps are generally associated with lower retention, but the relationship is system-dependent.

properties.name: First-cycle efficiency
properties.key_indicators_text: Carbon coating continuity (B2), exposed-Si/edge-plane area (A2, B1), surface-film formation (C2). BET may support powder comparisons but does not directly measure working-electrode electrochemical surface area.
properties.direction_of_effect: More exposed surface generally means more Li lost to SEI in the first cycle.

properties.name: Rate capability / fast charge
properties.key_indicators_text: Porosity and pore connectivity (D1, D2), orientation (D3), additive network (B4), particle size (B1).
properties.direction_of_effect: Open, low-tortuosity structures can favor high rate; orientation effects are system-dependent, and plating risk (E4) rises when transport and wetting are poor.

properties.name: Volumetric energy density
properties.direction_of_effect: Dense, low-void electrodes raise energy density but leave less swelling room.

properties.name: Gravimetric capacity
properties.key_indicators_text: Si fraction (A2), isolated Si (C3, B4), coating thickness (B2).
properties.direction_of_effect: Higher usable Si fraction raises capacity; isolated or over-coated Si lowers it.

properties.name: Internal resistance / impedance growth
properties.key_indicators_text: Contact gaps (C3), SEI and pore clogging (C2, E3), delamination (D8), cracks (D7).
properties.direction_of_effect: Growth in any of these raises impedance.

properties.name: Safety
properties.direction_of_effect: Plating is the main short-circuit route supported by the retrieved literature; defect and separator links were not verified and were removed.

properties.name: Manufacturing uniformity
properties.key_indicators_text: Thickness variation (D5), binder migration (C1), Si dispersion (A2).

architectures.name: Si/graphite blend (physical mixture)
architectures.typical_sem_signature: BSE: separate bright Si particles or clusters among dark graphite; Si largely uncoated and exposed.
architectures.main_trade_off: Good conductivity and easy processing; Si segregation and exposed Si surface. Commercial blends may contain ≲10 wt% Si, but composition is product-dependent.

verification.note: Si/graphite blending for commercialisation is well documented.

architectures.name: Si@C core–shell
architectures.typical_sem_signature: Spherical Si nanoparticles with a visible continuous carbon shell; no gap between core and shell.
architectures.main_trade_off: Better SEI stability and conductivity; a tight shell can crack as Si expands. Shell continuity and thickness should be confirmed by TEM when the shell is nanoscale.

verification.note: Si core / carbon shell designs and shell effects are supported.

architectures.name: Yolk–shell (Si@void@C)
architectures.typical_sem_signature: Broken or milled particles show a gap between the core and shell.
architectures.main_trade_off: Long cycle life; low tap density and volumetric capacity.

verification.note: Long cycling with a density/volumetric-capacity trade-off is reported.

architectures.name: Pomegranate-type (many Si nanoparticles in one carbon shell)
architectures.typical_sem_signature: Micron-sized spherical secondary particles with internal cavities; outer shell continuous.
architectures.main_trade_off: High tap density and stable SEI (shell outside); internal voids buffer expansion; more complex to make.

verification.note: Pomegranate design with stable SEI and high tap density.

architectures.name: Porous-carbon scaffold with Si deposited in pores
architectures.typical_sem_signature: Carbon particle surfaces look clean; Si is visible only in BSE/EDS inside pores.
architectures.main_trade_off: Built-in buffering and conduction; Si may be hidden from top-surface SEM, so use BSE/EDS and cross-sectioning to assess its distribution.

verification.note: Si deposited on/in carbon scaffolds is supported; 'clean carbon surface in SEM' observation was not directly found.

architectures.name: Si/C secondary particle (Si + graphite + pitch granulated)
architectures.typical_sem_signature: Rounded micron-scale granules with fine Si speckle embedded in a carbon matrix.
architectures.main_trade_off: Good packing and processability; Si fraction and contact depend on granulation.

verification.note: Granulated/composite Si-graphite secondary particles are reported.

architectures.name: SiOx/C
architectures.typical_sem_signature: Morphology similar to Si/C; oxide not visible by SEM (EDS shows O).
architectures.main_trade_off: Lower capacity, lower expansion and lower first-cycle efficiency than Si; may need prelithiation.

verification.note: Lower capacity/expansion, poorer first-cycle efficiency and prelithiation need are reported.

architectures.name: 1D/2D Si (nanowires, nanosheets, thin films) on carbon
architectures.typical_sem_signature: Fibre or sheet networks, visible interwoven structure.
architectures.main_trade_off: Good strain accommodation; low tap density.

verification.note: Nanowire/nanotube strain accommodation is supported; cost claim removed.

original.name: Surface defects of the coating
original.how_to_recognise_and_best_mode: Top view SE/ETD: pinholes, craters, scratches, protruding agglomerates, foreign particles.
original.what_to_measure: Defect density (per cm²) and size distribution; protruding height vs coating thickness.
original.verify_with_text: Optical inspection, EDS of foreign particles
original.favorable_state: Low density of defects, with no defects large enough to damage the separator or create local electrical/chemical hot spots.
original.unfavorable_state: Agglomerates larger than a fraction of the coating thickness (often ≳20–50 µm), pinholes, metal contaminants.
original.linked_properties_and_mechanism: Local hot spots, separator damage and internal short circuits, manufacturing yield.

deleted_items.name: Separator condition
deleted_items.reason: No work on separator post-mortem condition in Si/C cells was retrieved (query returned 0 works).

original.name: Separator condition
original.how_to_recognise_and_best_mode: Surface/cross-section of the cycled separator: clogged pores, embedded debris, local thinning or melting marks.
original.what_to_measure: Surface pore area fraction, foreign-particle count and size, penetration depth.
original.verify_with_text: Gurley number only as an auxiliary gas-permeability indicator; combine with wetting, impedance, permeability, or pore-structure measurements for ion transport.
original.favorable_state: Open, clean pores and intact thickness, with adequate electrolyte wetting.
original.unfavorable_state: Blocked pores, embedded Si/Li, punctures, or local thinning/melting.
